Korean makeup is less about covering the skin and more about making it look fresh. Popular Korean makeup pins on Pinterest tend to share the same parts: dewy skin, a soft pink flush high on the cheeks, a glow on the high points of the face and glossy lips.

This tutorial breaks that look into seven steps, with one product for each. Every pick comes from Olive Young Korea’s makeup sales ranking, checked on Nov. 22, 2026, and six of the seven are sold on Amazon US through the brand’s own store.

The look in one line

Thin dewy base, light shading, sheer blush right under the eyes, balm glow, soft pink eyes and a gradient gloss.

Before you start

  • Skin first. A dewy base sits better on moisturized skin. Our Korean cushion foundation guide covers prep and shade matching.
  • Go light, then build. Every step here works in thin layers. It is easier to add than to take away.
  • Match your undertone. Cool, pink-toned shades suit cool undertones. Peachy, warm shades suit warm undertones. Both versions of rom&nd’s contour and CLIO’s undertone shade guide help here.

The seven steps

  1. Base: a thin layer of cushion, tapped in.
  2. Contour: light shading under the cheekbones, along the jaw and at the sides of the nose.
  3. Blush: sheer pink, high on the cheeks, just under the eyes.
  4. Highlight: balm on the cheekbones, forehead center, nose bridge and chin.
  5. Eyes: a soft pink palette, with shimmer on the lid center and the aegyo-sal.
  6. Brows: soft and straight. See our Korean brow guide.
  7. Lips: a glossy gradient. Our Korean lip tint guide shows how to blur the edges.

The products for each step, with how to use them, are below.

Step 1, Base: JUNGSAEMMOOL Essential Skin Nuder Cushion

The dewy base this look is built on. JUNGSAEMMOOL describes it as a natural coverage cushion that adds a clear, radiant glow, and its lineup lists a natural glow finish.

No. 5 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants skin that looks like skin, with a soft sheen. The brand lists the dewy version for dry and combination skin.

How to use: Pick up a small amount and press a thin layer over the face, tapping it in. Build only where you need more coverage.

Step 2, Contour: rom&nd Better Than Contour

One compact with five shades for shading and soft definition. rom&nd makes two versions, #01 Neutral Warm and #02 Gray Cool, so you can match your undertone.

No. 8 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Beginners who want subtle shading without a harsh line. Choose Gray Cool for cool or pink undertones, Neutral Warm for warm or olive undertones.

How to use: With a puff or brush, sweep a light layer under the cheekbones, along the jaw and at the sides of the nose.

Step 3, Blush: NAMING. Fluffy Powder Blush

The sheer flush that makes this look Korean. NAMING. says it gives cheeks a natural look, as if lightly colored, with a soft, airy feel.

No. 30 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants a soft pink cheek. We could not find it on Amazon US, so buy it in Korea.

How to use: Tap a brush into the blush and sweep it high on the cheeks, starting just under the eyes and spreading out. Layer a deeper shade at the center if you want more color.

Step 4, Highlight: hince True Dimension Radiance Balm

A stick balm for the wet-looking glow on the high points of the face. hince calls it a multi-stick for highlight and blush, and says it can also be used on the eyes and lips.

No. 22 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants glow that melts into the skin rather than glitter on top.

How to use: Dab it on the cheekbones, the center of the forehead, the bridge of the nose and the chin, then blend with a fingertip so the warmth of your skin melts it in.

Step 5, Eyes: rom&nd Better Than Palette

Ten shades arranged so you can layer from light to deep. rom&nd describes the 06 Peony Nude Garden palette as a cool nude palette for soft, natural shading.

Two editions of this palette sat at No. 86 and No. 95 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants a full eye look in one palette. Pink and nude versions suit this soft pink look.

How to use: Sweep the lightest shade over the lid, a soft pink through the crease, and a deeper shade close to the lash line. Use a little shimmer on the center of the lid and on the aegyo-sal, the small puff under the eyes.

Step 5, Eyes (alternative): CLIO Pro Eye Palette Air

Twelve shades in one palette. CLIO describes the textures as airy matte, satin and shimmer that blend smoothly with even payoff, and publishes a shade guide by undertone.

No. 87 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants more shades to play with, or an all-matte version (CLIO's M20 and M21).

How to use: Use the matte shades for shading and the shimmer shades on the center of the lid and the aegyo-sal.

Step 7, Lips: fwee 3D Voluming Gloss

The glossy finish of this look. fwee describes it as juicy and glazed with a syrupy formula, in a 30% pigment version for a sheer layer and a 70% version for richer color.

No. 4 in Olive Young Korea's makeup ranking (checked Nov. 22, 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants a juicy lip. Pick the 30% pigment shades for a sheer, everyday look.

How to use: Apply the color to the center of the lips with the tip and blend outward, or layer it over a tint for a gradient lip.

The face map: where each step goes

  • Highlight: center of the forehead, bridge of the nose, tops of the cheekbones, cupid's bow and the center of the chin.
  • Contour: under the cheekbones, along the jaw, the sides of the nose and the hairline at the temples. Keep it light.
  • Blush: high on the cheeks, starting right under the eyes and spreading out toward the cheekbones. Soft edges, no circles.
  • Lips: deeper color at the center, blended out to the edges.

Where to buy

Six of the seven products are sold on Amazon US through the brands' own stores (checked Nov. 22, 2026). NAMING. Fluffy Powder Blush we could only find in Korea, at Olive Young. If you are visiting Seoul, our first Olive Young shopping list shows how to shop the store and claim a tax refund.

item.title: Korean Body Care Picks: Cream, Wash and Scrub
item.description: Korean body care worth a spot in your bag: a fragrance-free ceramide cream, a head-to-toe wash, a family-size lotion, the Italy towel, and how to pack them.
item.content:encoded:
For Korean body care, start with a fragrance-free ceramide cream like ILLIYOON's Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream for dry spots, plus a gentle wash and an Italy towel for weekly scrubbing. Apply cream to damp skin after a short warm shower, and pack anything over 100 mL in checked luggage.

Korean body care is less about fancy scents and more about big, plain basics. Shelves in Seoul are full of family-size lotions and pump washes, and the green Italy towel hangs nearby.

That makes a simple routine easy to build: wash gently, scrub once in a while, and seal in moisture with a thick cream. Here is what to pick and how to use it.

Who needs what

  • Dry, tight skin: a fragrance-free cream, not a thin lotion. The American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) says creams and ointments work better for dry skin.
  • Easily irritated skin: fewer products, no added fragrance, and patch-test anything new.
  • Rough elbows and knees: an occasional gentle scrub with an Italy towel, then cream.
  • Shared bathroom at home: one large bottle the whole family can use.

A shower routine that helps

  • Keep it short. The AAD suggests 5 to 10 minutes.
  • Use warm water, not hot.
  • Go light on cleanser. Use a mild one, only where you need it.
  • Moisturize within minutes, while your skin is still damp.

Where to shop

  • Korean beauty stores and drugstores carry the ILLIYOON line in several sizes. Compare sizes before you buy.
  • Amorepacific Mall is the brand group’s own online store, useful for checking sizes and current listings.

A weekly rhythm

  • Every day: a short warm shower, mild wash, cream on damp skin.
  • Once a week, at most: a long soak, a gentle pass with an Italy towel, then a generous layer of cream. Seoul bathhouse scrub attendants told CNN Travel that scrubbing more often risks over-exfoliation.
  • If skin stings or turns red: skip the scrub and keep the cream.

Best for Dry, Sensitive Skin: ILLIYOON Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream

A thick cream from ILLIYOON, an Amorepacific brand, labeled for sensitive and dry skin. The tube reads "Fragrance Free," "9 FREE" and vegan, with soy-ceramide and madecassoside called out on the front. The big tube makes sense for elbows, shins and hands, where body skin often feels driest.

Listed in the National Eczema Association's Seal of Acceptance product directory (checked Nov. 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone with dry or easily irritated body skin, and anyone avoiding added fragrance. If you have a skin condition, ask a dermatologist first.

How to use: After a short, warm shower, smooth it onto skin that is still damp. Reapply on rough spots whenever they feel tight.

Two more from the same shelf

  • ILLIYOON Ceramide Ato Lotion: the lighter, pump-bottle partner to the cream. Amorepacific Mall lists it under body care in 564 ml bottles and showed it at No. 3 in its weekly body care ranking when we checked (Nov. 16, 2026).
  • ILLIYOON Ceramide Ato 6.0 Top to Toe Wash: a wash named for head-to-toe use, sold in 500 ml and 1,000 ml sizes at Amorepacific Mall. Read the label for where to use it.
  • Italy towel (이태리타월): the green scrub mitt Korean bathhouses use. Light and easy to pack. Read our Italy towel guide before you use it.

Words on the label

  • 바디워시 (ba-di-wo-si): body wash.
  • 바디로션 (ba-di-ro-syeon): body lotion.
  • 바디크림 (ba-di-keu-rim): body cream.
  • 무향 (mu-hyang): no scent. The AAD notes "unscented" products may contain masking chemicals, so look for "fragrance free" if scent bothers your skin.
  • 민감 (min-gam): sensitive.
  • 대용량 (dae-yong-ryang): large size.

Packing body care home

Carry-on limit: each liquid, cream or gel must be 3.4 oz (100 mL) or less, in one quart-size bag (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: TSA). Rules can change, so check before you fly.

  • Big tubs go in checked bags. Tape the caps and put each in a zip bag.
  • Leave room. Family-size bottles are heavy. Weigh your bag before the airport.

item.title: Korean Hair Treatment Guide: What to Buy and How to Use
item.description: Korean hair treatments for visitors: rinse-off treatments, protein and ceramide formulas, hair packs, how they differ from conditioner, and how to use them.
item.content:encoded:
A Korean hair treatment is usually a rinse-off cream or liquid you use after shampoo, much like a richer conditioner or a quick hair mask. Look for proteins like hydrolyzed keratin or lipids like ceramide on the label, leave it on for a few minutes, then rinse.

Hair care is the third most popular category for foreign shoppers at Olive Young, after skincare and makeup, the chain said in August 2026. Foreign shoppers made up about 18% of its hair care sales from January to August.

Korean shelves can be confusing, though. You will see treatments, packs, ampoules and water treatments next to conditioner. Here is what each one is, and how to use it.

What a “treatment” is in Korea

  • Treatment (트리트먼트): usually a rinse-off cream or liquid you use after shampoo. It is often richer than conditioner and stays on for a few minutes.
  • Hair pack or mask (헤어팩): a thicker rinse-off product for a longer weekly session.
  • Water treatment: a thin, liquid rinse-off formula.
  • Conditioner: the lighter everyday step. Some brands sell it separately and suggest pairing it with their treatment.

Protein or ceramide: read the label

  • Protein treatments list ingredients such as hydrolyzed keratin, silk or soy protein. La’dor’s Hydro LPP Treatment lists all three.
  • Ceramide formulas list ceramide NP or similar. Cosmetics Europe’s COSMILE database lists ceramide NP as a hair-conditioning ingredient, one that makes hair easier to comb and gives it a softer, shinier look.
  • Oils show up too: La’dor lists olive and jojoba oils, and Aromatica lists argan oil.

Who should use which

  • Bleached, permed or heat-styled hair: start with a protein treatment.
  • Fine hair that goes flat: try a liquid water treatment, and keep it off your roots.
  • Dry, frizzy ends: a cream treatment or a weekly hair pack.
  • Oily scalp, dry ends: treatment on the lengths only, plus a scalp product. See our Korean scalp care guide.

How to use a rinse-off treatment

  • Shampoo first. Then squeeze out as much water as you can.
  • Apply to the lengths. Work from mid-lengths to ends, where hair is driest.
  • Wait. Aromatica’s directions for its 3-in-1 treatment say 2 to 3 minutes. Hair packs can stay on longer if the label says so.
  • Rinse well. Leftover product can make hair feel heavy.
  • Heavy packs: follow the label for how long and how often.

Where to shop in Seoul

  • Olive Young: 151 of its stores sat in what it calls global tourist districts as of August 2026. Those stores put staff who speak foreign languages on the floor first and post signs in several languages.
  • Brand stores online: La’dor, Moremo and Aromatica each run their own web stores, handy for checking sizes and full ingredient lists before you go.
  • Compare two stores: foreign shoppers surveyed in its tourist-district stores in May 2026 said they visited 2.8 stores on average. Prices and sale items can differ.

Read the back label first

  • Rinse-off or leave-in: the directions tell you which. Leave-in products go on towel-dried hair and stay in.
  • Protein near the top: a sign the formula leans on protein.
  • Fragrance: most of these list it. Skip them if scent bothers you.

Below: three Korean treatments to look for, the Korean words to know, and how to pack them.

Three treatments to look for

  • Protein treatment: La'dor Hydro LPP Treatment. La'dor's Korean store calls it a protein treatment for damaged hair and lists hydrolyzed keratin, soy protein, silk and conchiolin protein, with olive and jojoba oils. The 530 ml bottle is ₩19,500 there.
  • Water treatment: Moremo's line is named for it. The current version on Moremo's Korean store is the Ampoule Water Treatment Miracle 100, sold in 200 ml and 400 ml. It is an option if creams feel heavy on your hair.
  • Cream 3-in-1: Aromatica Rosemary 3-In-1 Treatment, 160 ml. Aromatica describes it as a silicone-free cream for hydration, nourishment and shine, with hydrolyzed corn, soy and wheat proteins plus hyaluronic acid.

Prices change often and sales are frequent, so compare the brand store with Olive Young before you pay.

Korean words on the bottle

  • 트리트먼트 (teu-ri-teu-meon-teu): treatment.
  • 헤어팩 (he-eo-paek): hair pack, a mask.
  • 단백질 (dan-baek-jil): protein.
  • 손상모 (son-sang-mo): damaged hair.
  • 워터 트리트먼트: water treatment, a liquid formula.
  • 씻어내는 / 씻어내지 않는: rinse-off / leave-in.

Before you pack it

  • Big bottles go in checked bags. Korean treatments often come in 500 ml sizes or larger. Liquids and creams count as liquids at airport security.
  • Bag it. Put pump bottles in a zip bag in case the pump opens in your suitcase.
  • Buy the smaller size first. Moremo sells its water treatment in 200 ml as well as 400 ml, so you can see how your hair likes it before you commit to a big bottle.

item.title: Korean Skincare Steps, Simply Explained
item.description: The real order of Korean skincare steps, from thin to thick, what each step does, and a 3-step minimum you can keep on a busy travel morning.
item.content:encoded:
Korean skincare steps go from thinnest to thickest: cleanser, toner, serum, moisturizer, then sunscreen in the morning. The minimum is three steps, cleanser, moisturizer and sunscreen, and you add a toner or serum only when you want more hydration or a specific look.

The “10-step Korean routine” made K-beauty famous. You do not need it. Round Lab, a Korean skincare brand, writes that it was always more of a Western marketing story than a daily Korean habit.

What matters is the order, and knowing what each step is for. Then you can keep three steps or ten.

The one rule: thin to thick

Cleveland Clinic says a routine should go from lightest to heaviest. A watery layer goes under a thick cream, never the other way around. Two exceptions:

  • Sunscreen goes last in the morning, after your other skincare and before makeup. Cleveland Clinic and the American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) both put it at the end.
  • Anything a doctor gave you goes on right after cleansing, the AAD says. Their instructions come first.

Each step, in plain terms

  • Oil cleanser (night, optional): dissolves makeup and sunscreen. Round Lab suggests it first at night if you wore either. Not everyone agrees: a Cleveland Clinic dermatologist advises cleansing once.
  • Cleanser: clears away dirt and grime so the next steps can do their job.
  • Toner: in K-beauty, toner is a hydrating step, not an astringent, Round Lab says. Pat it on right after cleansing.
  • Essence: a light hydrating layer, and the easiest step to skip. Round Lab says two or three layers of a hydrating toner can cover toner, essence and a light serum.
  • Serum or ampoule: a more concentrated step for one goal, such as a brighter, more even-looking tone. Cleveland Clinic suggests one serum at a time. Round Lab calls ampoules “rescue products, not daily staples.”
  • Eye cream (optional): goes between serum and moisturizer. Use your ring finger, the AAD says, because it pulls least on thin skin.
  • Moisturizer: seals in hydration and helps keep skin from drying out.
  • Sunscreen (morning): the final skincare step. Cleveland Clinic recommends broad-spectrum SPF 15 or higher.

Why the order matters

A thin serum under a thick cream can reach your skin. Put the cream on first, and the serum has a harder time getting through, Cleveland Clinic explains. That is the whole logic behind thin to thick.

Common mix-ups

  • Moving sunscreen earlier because it feels thinner than your cream. It still goes last in the morning.
  • Stacking serums. Cleveland Clinic suggests one serum at a time.
  • Piling on anti-aging products. The AAD warns this can irritate skin.
  • Oil cleansing every morning. Round Lab suggests the oil step at night, when you have makeup or sunscreen to remove.

Three routines to copy

  • The minimum (3 steps): cleanser, moisturizer, sunscreen. Cleveland Clinic calls this the least you want to do.
  • The K-beauty basic (4 steps): cleanser, hydrating toner, moisturizer, sunscreen. This is the four-step base Round Lab describes.
  • The longer night (6 steps): oil cleanser, cleanser, toner, serum or ampoule, eye cream, moisturizer.

On a trip

  • Pack the minimum. Three products cover a travel morning.
  • Shop for one step at a time. Pick the step you want to add, then compare products for that step only.
  • Sheet masks are optional. Save them for a night when you have time.

Add one step at a time

More is not always better. The AAD warns that using too many products may irritate skin, especially more than one anti-aging product.

  • Add one new product and give it time before adding the next.
  • Patch test first. The AAD suggests a quarter-sized spot on the inside of your arm, twice a day for 7 to 10 days. Red, itchy or swollen skin means stop.
  • Keep what you can see working. Drop a step that does nothing you can notice.

Morning vs. night

  • Morning: cleanser, toner (optional), serum (optional), moisturizer, sunscreen.
  • Night: oil cleanser if you wore makeup or sunscreen, cleanser, toner, serum, moisturizer.
  • Retinol: Cleveland Clinic suggests using it at night in place of a serum. If yours is a prescription, follow your doctor, not this list.

Find each step in a Korean store

Korean shops group products by step. These are the category names on Round Lab's Korean store:

  • 클렌징 (keul-len-jing): cleansing.
  • 토너/미스트 (to-neo/mi-seu-teu): toner and mist.
  • 에센스/앰플 (e-sen-seu/aem-peul): essence and ampoule.
  • 로션/크림 (ro-syeon/keu-rim): lotion and cream.
  • 선 케어 (seon ke-eo): sun care.

Shopping for one step? Show the word to a staff member.

item.title: Gyeongju Day Trip: King Munmu's Sea Tomb and Silla Sites
item.description: A Gyeongju day trip from Seoul by KTX, built around King Munmu of the new drama Munmu: his tomb in the sea, Gameunsa and Wolji Pond at night.
item.content:encoded:
Take the KTX from Seoul Station to Gyeongju Station, about 2 hours 10 minutes by Gyeongju City's count. Spend the day on the east coast, where King Munmu's tomb sits in the sea off Bonggil Beach, see the twin pagodas at Gameunsa Temple Site, then return to town for Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond lit up at night.

Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom. Today it is a small city of royal tombs, temple sites and palace ponds, about two hours from Seoul by train.

More foreign visitors are making the trip. Gyeongju City counted 707,197 foreign visitors from January to June 2026, up 19.0% from a year earlier, based on Korea Tourism Data Lab figures (reported Aug. 20, 2026).

There is a new reason to go, too. Munmu, a KBS2 historical drama about the wars of Korea’s Three Kingdoms, premiered on Nov. 14, 2026, and is streaming on Netflix. Its title king, Munmu, ruled Silla from 661 to 681. This guide follows the places tied to him, from his tomb in the sea to the palace pond dug in his reign.

Who was King Munmu?

  • The king: Munmu ruled Silla from 661 to 681, the Korea Heritage Service says.
  • His last wish: the Samguk Sagi, an early history of Korea’s Three Kingdoms, records that he asked to be cremated and buried in the East Sea. The Korea Heritage Service says he wanted to become a dragon and guard the kingdom from Japanese raiders. Treat the dragon part as legend.
  • His son: King Sinmun finished the temple his father started and built a pavilion facing the sea tomb. Both are on this route.

Getting there from Seoul

  • KTX train: high-speed KTX trains run from Seoul Station to Gyeongju Station. Gyeongju City puts the trip at about 2 hours 10 minutes. Times vary by train, so check the Korail timetable.
  • The station name: Gyeongju Station is the former Singyeongju Station, the KTX stop outside downtown. Older maps may still show the old name.
  • From the station to town: buses 700 and 710 run from Gyeongju Station to the Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond stop in about 25 minutes, the Gyeongju National Museum says.
  • To the coast: the King Munmu sites are on the east coast. Gyeongju City lists buses 150, 150-1 and 1150 from the Express Bus Terminal downtown to the Daejonggyo stop, then about a 10-minute walk to the marine museum. A taxi saves time if you are short on hours.

The King Munmu route

  1. Munmu Daewang Marine History Museum. Start here to get the story before you see the sea. Gyeongju City lists hours of 10:00 to 18:00 from March to October and 10:00 to 17:00 from November to February. It is closed on Mondays, Jan. 1, and on Seollal and Chuseok days. Adult tickets are ₩3,000, but entry is free until Dec. 31, 2026 (as of Nov. 22, 2026. Source: Gyeongju City).
  2. Igyeondae Pavilion. A three-minute walk from the museum, Gyeongju City says. King Sinmun built a pavilion here, at the spot with the best view of his father’s sea tomb. The building you see today was rebuilt on the excavated site. Legend says Sinmun received a flute called Manpasikjeok here, from a dragon. The story comes from the Samguk Yusa, a later collection of history and legend.
  3. Tomb of King Munmu (Daewangam). A rock formation about 200 meters off the shore at Bonggil Beach, about five minutes by car from the museum. The Korea Heritage Service lists it as the king’s underwater tomb, designated a Historic Site in 1967. Stand on the beach and look out at the rocks.
  4. Gameunsa Temple Site. King Munmu began this temple to guard against Japanese raiders, and King Sinmun completed it in 682, the Korea Heritage Service says. The name means a temple of gratitude. Only the stone foundations and two three-story stone pagodas remain, and the pagodas are a National Treasure. Legend says a channel under the main hall let the dragon king come in from the sea.
  5. Back to town: Gyeongju National Museum. If you arrive before 18:00, stop in. The permanent galleries are free, the museum says. It holds fragments of King Munmu’s stone monument, which records his cremation and sea burial.
  6. Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond at night. The Samguk Sagi says the pond was dug in 674, during Munmu’s reign. Three buildings were restored in 1980, and at night their lights reflect in the water. VisitKorea lists hours of 09:00 to 22:00, with last entry at 21:30, open every day. Adult tickets are ₩3,000 (as of Nov. 22, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).

Day trip or overnight?

  • Day trip: take an early KTX, do the coast in the morning and early afternoon, and finish at Wolji Pond. Check the last KTX back to Seoul before you go.
  • One night: stay downtown, see Wolji Pond after dark without watching the clock, and give the national museum a full morning the next day.

Small tips

  • Wear walking shoes. The temple site and the pond paths are mostly gravel and dirt.
  • Go to Wolji Pond after sunset. The buildings are lit at night, and the pond is open until 22:00.
  • Carry some cash. Small shops near the coast may prefer it.

Read next

If you are planning more of Korea after Gyeongju, our Busan travel guide is a natural next stop south. For your first days in the capital, start with our Seoul first trip tips.

Before you go

  • Book the train early. KTX seats from Seoul fill up on weekends. Check times and book on the Korail website or app.
  • Plan the coast first. The tomb, Igyeondae and Gameunsa are on the east coast, far from downtown. Go there in the daylight and save Wolji Pond for the evening.
  • Check closing days. The Munmu Daewang Marine History Museum closes on Mondays. The Gyeongju National Museum has a regular closing day on the second Monday of March, June, September and December.
  • Use a Korean map app. Naver Map or KakaoMap shows bus numbers and stops better than Google Maps in Korea.

About the drama Munmu

Munmu is a 28-episode KBS2 historical drama about the leaders of Korea's Three Kingdoms at war. It premiered on Nov. 14, 2026, and is also on Netflix. KBS said it reached No. 1 on Netflix's Top 10 TV list in South Korea on Nov. 17, 2026 (Source: Sports Kyunghyang). This guide is not affiliated with KBS or Netflix, and we use no images from the drama.

item.title: Korean Cushion Foundation: A Beginner's Guide
item.description: What a Korean cushion foundation is, how to read shades like 21N, pick dewy or matte, press it on with the puff, and save money with refills.
item.content:encoded:
A Korean cushion foundation is liquid foundation soaked into a sponge inside a compact, which you press onto skin with a puff. Pick your shade by number and undertone letter (for example 21N), choose a dewy or matte finish, and buy a set with a refill to save money.

The cushion compact is a Korean idea. Amorepacific launched the first one, the IOPE Air Cushion, in 2008, and says its cushions passed 100 million units sold worldwide by 2016.

It works like a stamp pad. A sponge soaked in liquid foundation sits in a compact, and you press it onto your face with a puff. Amorepacific says the idea came from parking-lot stamps and from customers who wanted a light lotion with UV protection and makeup in one.

Is a cushion right for you?

  • You want light, fast coverage. A cushion takes a minute and fits in a small bag.
  • You touch up during the day. The puff and mirror are built in.
  • You want full coverage. Pick a cover or matte cushion and build in thin layers.
  • You love a bare face. Try a dewy cushion and use it only where you need it.

How to read Korean shades

Korean shade codes pair a number with a letter, like 21N or 17C1. On HERA’s shade chart, shades ending in C sit under “Cool, bright rosy,” N under “Neutral” and W under “Warm, soft golden undertone.” HERA’s chart runs from 13N1 to 27N1.

  • Start with 21N if you’re unsure. Amorepacific says 21N is the most popular shade, because it subtly brightens and blends easily.
  • Swatch on your jaw, not your hand. Your face and hand are often different colors.
  • Check the range. Some lines go deeper than others. Ask staff for the deepest shade if 25 or 27 is too light.

Popular cushions on Seoul shelves

These were in Olive Young Korea’s makeup sales ranking on Nov. 16, 2026. Prices are list prices for sets with a refill, and many were on sale for less.

  • April Skin Magic Snow Cushion 4.0 (#1), ₩33,000. Sold as main product plus refill.
  • Naming Layered Fit Cushion (#4), ₩34,000. A refill set.
  • Jung Saem Mool Essential Skin Nuder Cushion (#5), ₩48,000. Main product plus refill.
  • VDL Cover Stain Perfecting Cushion (#8), ₩36,000. A set with a refill.
  • HERA Black Cushion (#13), ₩74,000. Ten shades in a main-plus-refill set. Amorepacific says the line launched in 2017 and passed 10 million units sold by February 2024.

On a budget

Daiso sells 15 g cushions for ₩5,000, like the Tag Dewy Skin Cushion, which showed 6,400+ purchases on Daiso Mall (Nov. 16, 2026). It is a cheap way to see if you like the format before you spend more. If you love it, move up to an Olive Young cushion with a refill.

One note on SPF

Many cushions list an SPF. You usually apply a thin layer of cushion, so keep your regular sunscreen underneath. Our Korean sunscreen guide covers what to pick.

How to apply a cushion with the puff

  • Prep first. Finish skincare and sunscreen, then wait a minute so the base doesn't slide.
  • Load lightly. Press the puff onto the sponge once or twice. Too much at once looks heavy.
  • Press, don't swipe. Tap the puff on your cheeks, then spread outward to your forehead, nose and chin.
  • Build where you need it. Add a second tap only on redness or spots.
  • Fold the puff for edges. Fold it in half to reach the sides of your nose and under your eyes.
  • Wash the puff. Rinse it with mild soap and let it dry fully, or keep a spare.

Dewy or matte?

Dewy (glow, 윤광): a shinier finish. Amorepacific links glow cushions to the trend for a natural, radiant complexion from 2017 to 2019.

Matte (매트) or semi-matte: less shine and more hold. Amorepacific notes that matte cushions grew in 2020 to 2022 because they didn't transfer onto face masks.

Not sure? Since 2023, Amorepacific says glow and matte have shared the top of the charts, so pick by your skin and the weather. Dry skin often likes dewy. Oily skin in a Seoul summer may prefer matte.

Refills and how to shop them

  • Look for 본품+리필. It means main product plus refill. Many Olive Young cushions are sold this way.
  • Keep the case. Amorepacific says it offers refillable cushions as standard, so you can buy refills alone later.
  • Match the brand. A refill fits only its own case. Buy the same line and shade code.
  • Pack it flat. A cushion is small and light. Keep it closed in a zip bag in case the compact pops open.

item.title: Italy Towel: How to Use Korea's Body Scrub Mitt
item.description: What the Korean Italy towel is, why it is named after Italy, how to use it safely at home, and what to expect from a seshin scrub at a Korean bathhouse.
item.content:encoded:
An Italy towel is a coarse Korean scrub mitt, first made in Busan in 1967 from rough rayon fabric imported from Italy. Soak first, scrub body skin with light strokes, moisturize right after, and keep it to about once a week, the limit Seoul bathhouse scrub attendants suggest.

In Korea you will find small, scratchy mitts, usually green, near the soap. That is the Italy towel, or 이태리타월. Koreans use it to scrub dead skin from the body, at home and at the bathhouse.

It looks simple, and it is. The skill is in using it gently.

Why “Italy”?

  • Made in Busan. Busan Ilbo reports that Hanil Textile in Busan’s Choeup-dong made the first Italy towels in 1967.
  • Italian fabric. The company had imported rayon from Italy that turned out too rough to use, so it tried the cloth as a scrub towel.
  • Slow start. Early sales were weak, Busan Ilbo notes, because many people still scrubbed with stones.
  • Now everywhere. It became a household item in Korea and a staple at Korean saunas, Wikipedia notes.

Busan, the bath city

  • Lots of bathhouses. Busan Ilbo, citing the bathhouse magazine Jip-ap Mogyoktang (집앞목욕탕), says Busan once had about 1,500 public baths and still runs about 500, roughly as many as Seoul.
  • A second invention. The same report credits a Busan machine shop with an automatic back scrubber in the early 1980s: a spinning disc fitted with an Italy towel.

How it works

The mitt has no grains or chemicals. It works by friction. Warm water softens the top layer of skin, and the coarse weave lifts it off in gray rolls, which is why the habit goes with a long soak.

How to use it at home

  • Soak first. Wikipedia, citing a Vogue writer, advises several minutes in water before you start. Bathhouse attendants told CNN about 30 minutes.
  • Wet the mitt. Never scrub dry skin.
  • Use short, light strokes. That is the AAD’s advice for any brush or sponge. Pink, not red, is the goal.
  • Work by area. Legs, arms, then back. Skip the face, chest and any thin or broken skin.
  • Rinse, then moisturize. The AAD says to apply moisturizer right after exfoliating, since it can dry skin.
  • Once a week at most. Seoul scrub attendants told CNN more often risks over-exfoliation.

Signs to stop

  • Stinging or bright redness. You are pressing too hard.
  • Raw or shiny patches. Stop and let skin rest.
  • Irritation that lasts. See a dermatologist.

At a bathhouse: the seshin scrub

Many jjimjilbang (찜질방) and neighborhood bathhouses offer a paid body scrub called seshin (세신). CNN Travel describes it like this:

  • Separate areas: men and women bathe separately and are scrubbed by attendants of their own gender.
  • Soak first: about 30 minutes, in water at a temperature you are comfortable with.
  • Bar soap before, not body wash: attendants say liquid wash makes skin too slippery.
  • Fully bare: remove rings, earrings and glasses, and bring a hair tie.
  • About 40 minutes on a plastic table, then a rinse.
  • Scrub first, sauna after, the attendants advise.

Prices are posted at the bath area or counter. Ask for 세신 (se-shin).

Who should skip it or go gently

  • Sensitive, dry or acne-prone skin: the AAD says a washcloth and a mild exfoliator may suit you better than a coarse tool.
  • Darker skin tones or dark spots: the AAD advises avoiding strong mechanical exfoliation.
  • Retinoid, retinol or benzoyl peroxide users: scrubbing on top can add dryness.
  • Cuts, sunburn, fresh shaving or waxing: wait until skin is calm.
  • Any skin condition: ask a dermatologist first.

Buying one in Korea

  • Color: green is the standard. Pink is softer and blue is coarser, according to Wikipedia, citing a Vogue writer. Start soft.
  • Shape: most are two squares sewn into a mitt that fits over your hand.
  • Words to ask for: 이태리타월 (i-tae-ri ta-wol) or 때수건 (ttae-su-geon), scrub towel.
  • Pack it dry. It weighs almost nothing and has no liquid limit.

item.title: What Is Cica? Centella Asiatica, Explained
item.description: What cica means in Korean skincare: the Centella asiatica plant, the ingredient names to find on a label, Korean words for the store, and how to patch test.
item.content:encoded:
Cica is the K-beauty nickname for Centella asiatica, a small plant also called gotu kola or tiger grass. On a label, look for Centella Asiatica Extract, Madecassoside, Asiaticoside, Asiatic Acid or Madecassic Acid. Skincare brands use it for a soothing, comfortable feel.

In Korean skincare, “cica” is shorthand for one plant: Centella asiatica. Amorepacific, the Korean beauty group, notes that the plant is often called cica in cosmetics.

You will see the word on toners, creams and masks. Here is what it is, how to find it on a label, and how to try it safely.

The plant

  • What it is: a perennial plant in the Apiaceae family, the plant family of parsley and carrots.
  • Where it grows: India, Pakistan, Madagascar and equatorial Africa, among other places, a 2013 review in Postepy Dermatologii i Alergologii says.
  • Other names: gotu kola, tiger grass and Indian pennywort. In Korean, 병풀 (byeong-pul).
  • What is in it: four main compounds called pentacyclic triterpenes: asiaticoside, madecassoside, asiatic acid and madecassic acid.

How to spot it on an ingredient list

The word “cica” on the front does not tell you what is inside. The ingredient list does. Look for these names:

  • Centella Asiatica Extract: the standard name for the plant extract.
  • Centella Asiatica Leaf Extract: or another plant-part version. Amorepacific lists leaf and stem forms.
  • Madecassoside: one compound purified from the plant. Hwahae notes it often appears next to Centella Asiatica Extract.
  • Asiaticoside, Asiatic Acid, Madecassic Acid: the other three main compounds.
  • On Korean labels: 병풀추출물 (centella extract), 마데카소사이드 (madecassoside), 아시아티코사이드 (asiaticoside).

One product may list several of these. Another may list only one. Both can be called cica.

Cica on the front, centella in the list?

  • Not always the same thing. Some brands use “cica” in a product or blend name. Round Lab, for example, describes its Pine Calming Cica Ampoule as using its own “Pine Cica Activer.” Check the list for the centella names above.
  • Extract or one compound. A product with only Madecassoside uses one purified compound. One with Centella Asiatica Extract uses the plant extract, which holds several compounds, Hwahae explains.
  • Look for specifics. Amorepacific says a product that states how its four main compounds are standardized gives you a better sense of what is inside.

What it does, in cosmetic terms

  • A soothing feel. Skincare brands use centella for a soothing, comfortable feel on sensitive-feeling skin, Hwahae notes.
  • Softer-feeling skin. Formulas often pair it with panthenol and ceramides for a soft, smooth finish.
  • Slow and steady. Amorepacific says changes are gradual, so give a product time.

What cica is not

  • Not medicine. A cica cream is a cosmetic. It makes no promise about any skin condition.
  • Not right for everyone. Some people react to it. Patch test first, as below.
  • Have a skin problem? Ask a dermatologist or a pharmacist, not a shelf label.

Who it suits, per Hwahae

  • Sensitive-feeling skin that wants a gentle, comfortable step.
  • Dry or rough-feeling skin, often in a cream with ceramides.
  • Anyone layering actives like retinol or niacinamide who wants a calm-feeling partner step.

Patch test before you commit

The AAD's method, for any new product:

  • Where: a quarter-sized spot that won't get rubbed or washed, like the inside of your arm or the bend of your elbow.
  • How long: twice a day for 7 to 10 days, using your normal amount.
  • Watch for: red, itchy or swollen skin. If you see it, gently wash the product off and stop using it.
  • Plant allergies: if you react to plants in the Apiaceae family, Amorepacific suggests asking a specialist before you try cica.

Where cica shows up

  • Forms: you will find it in serums, creams and ampoules, Hwahae notes.
  • Common partners: panthenol and ceramides, for a soft, smooth feel.
  • With other actives: it is generally used alongside retinol or niacinamide. Add one new active at a time.
  • Give it time: Amorepacific says any change is gradual, so steady use matters more than a big first impression.

Words to know in a Korean store

  • 시카 (si-ka): cica.
  • 병풀 (byeong-pul): the Korean name for Centella asiatica.
  • 병풀추출물: Centella asiatica extract, as it appears on Korean ingredient lists.
  • 진정 (jin-jeong): soothing. Round Lab's Korean store has a 민감/진정 (sensitive and soothing) category.

Point to the word on your phone if you need help finding a shelf.
