item.title: Korean Perfume Hand Cream: Why Visitors Buy It
item.description: What a Korean perfume hand cream is, why visitors fill bags with them at Olive Young, and how to pick a scent, a size and a gift without guessing.
item.content:encoded:
A Korean perfume hand cream is a hand cream sold mainly on its scent, often in numbered fragrances that match a brand's perfume line. Visitors buy them as easy gifts, and Olive Young says foreign tourists made up about 40% of its hand care sales in 2026, with BEYOND, Hetras and W.DRESSROOM especially popular.

Hand cream is one of the easiest things to buy in a Korean beauty store, and visitors buy a lot of it. In an Aug. 31, 2026 press release, CJ Olive Young said foreign tourists made up about 40% of its hand care sales, and called the category a go-to travel souvenir.

The same release named the hand creams doing best with visitors: perfume hand creams from BEYOND, Hetras and W.DRESSROOM. Here is what that label means and how to pick one in the store.

What makes it a “perfume” hand cream

  • The scent leads. You choose it the way you would choose a perfume, by smell first.
  • Scents come with numbers. W.DRESSROOM numbers its scents, such as No.49 Peach Blossom, and uses the same scent names in its perfume line and its hand creams.
  • It still works as hand cream. W.DRESSROOM describes its version as a non-sticky, lightweight cream that keeps hands moist and soft.

Why visitors buy it

  • Easy gift. Olive Young itself describes hand care as a good category for travel souvenirs and gifts.
  • No skin-type guessing. You pick a scent, not a formula for someone else’s face.
  • Small and light. A tube slips into a gift bag or a coat pocket.
  • Easy to try. Smell a tester on the shelf, or ask staff for one.

How to pick one in the store

  • Test on your skin. Put a little on the back of your hand and wait a minute before you decide.
  • Match the scent to the person. Soft, clean scents are a safe pick when you don’t know someone’s taste.
  • Read the label if you’re sensitive. Fragrance is listed as an ingredient. If your skin reacts to scent, try a small area first, or choose an unscented hand cream.
  • Ask for the tax refund. Purchases of ₩15,000 or more at participating stores can qualify (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea). Bring your passport.

Who it suits

  • Good fit: gift lists, coworkers, a host, anyone who likes a signature scent.
  • Think twice: people who avoid fragrance, or friends with very sensitive skin.

Where to buy

  • In Korea: Olive Young, which named all three brands in its visitor sales release. Compare the scents on the tester shelf before you pick, and buy an extra tube if you liked one for yourself.
  • Back home: W.DRESSROOM sells its hand cream on an official US online store, in a smaller 50 ml tube.

Best for an Easy Gift: W.DRESSROOM Perfume Hand Cream

It is one of the three perfume hand cream brands Olive Young named as especially popular with visitors. The brand describes the cream as non-sticky and lightweight, made to keep hands moist and soft. Scents carry numbers, so it is easy to remember the one you liked and find it again.

Olive Young named W.DRESSROOM among the perfume hand cream brands that are especially popular with foreign visitors (CJ Olive Young press release, Aug. 31, 2026).

Who it suits: Coworkers, a host family, a friend who likes a scent. Skip it for anyone who avoids fragrance.

How to use: Rub a small amount into clean, dry hands. Scents include No.49 Peach Blossom, which the brand describes as the fresh scent of sweet peach juice, plus No.30 White Musk and No.97 April Cotton. Smell the tester first.

The three brands Olive Young named

BEYOND, Hetras and W.DRESSROOM are the perfume hand cream brands Olive Young called especially popular in its Aug. 31, 2026 release. It listed them in Korean alphabetical order and did not rank them.

  • W.DRESSROOM: the tube pictured above. It also runs an official US online store, so you can reorder at home.
  • Hetras: sells a perfume hand cream on its official Korean site.
  • BEYOND: sells hand cream sets on its official Korean site.

If the store carries all three, smell each one before you choose. The scent is the whole point.

Packing and the tax refund

  • Checked bag is simplest. Tubes are light, and you skip the carry-on liquids question. If you pack them in a carry-on, check the TSA liquids rule before you fly.
  • Keep them sealed. Tax refund items must be new, unopened and unused (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea). Open your own tube after you land.
  • Bundle small buys. A refund needs a purchase of at least ₩15,000 at a participating store (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea). Several tubes bought together go on one receipt.

Our tax refund guide walks through each step.

Say it in Korean

  • "테스트해 봐도 돼요?" (te-seu-teu-hae bwa-do dwae-yo?) Can I try the tester?
  • "향 추천해 주세요." (hyang chu-cheon-hae ju-se-yo.) Please recommend a scent.
  • "선물 포장 돼요?" (seon-mul po-jang dwae-yo?) Can you gift wrap it?

Show the product on your phone if the words don't come out.

item.title: How to Choose a Korean Sunscreen: SPF and PA
item.description: What SPF50+ and PA++++ mean on a Korean sunscreen, how they compare with US Broad Spectrum labels, and how to pick a texture in Seoul or at home.
item.content:encoded:
Read two marks on a Korean sunscreen: SPF, which rates UVB protection, and PA, a four-step UVA grade where PA++++ is the highest. US versions say Broad Spectrum instead of PA, and the formula can differ, so read the box you are actually buying.

Korean sunscreen boxes carry two marks. Most US tubes carry one. Learn what each means and you will pick the right tube in a minute, in Seoul or at home.

What the Korean label tells you

  • SPF: rates protection from UVB rays, says Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS). Anything that tests at SPF 50 or higher is labeled “SPF50+” (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: MFDS).
  • PA: the grade for UVA protection. It runs PA+, PA++, PA+++ and PA++++. More plus signs mean higher UVA protection.
  • 기능성화장품 (functional cosmetic): in Korea, sunscreen is a cosmetic with a function defined by law. Each product must pass an MFDS evaluation or be reported to it. The MFDS tells shoppers to look for this mark.

What the US label tells you

  • Broad Spectrum: the product passed an FDA test for both UVA and UVB protection.
  • SPF number: mainly a measure of UVB protection, the FDA says.
  • Water resistant (40 or 80 minutes): how long it stays effective while you swim or sweat (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: FDA). No sunscreen is waterproof.
  • Drug Facts: in the US, sunscreen is regulated as a drug, so active ingredients are listed with percentages.

PA++++ vs. Broad Spectrum

They are different tests. PA is a graded scale built on a UVA method developed in Japan and now widely used in Asian markets, a 2026 review in Cureus notes. Broad Spectrum is pass or fail.

So a Korean tube with PA++++ tells you how high its UVA grade is. A US tube tells you only that it passed.

Pick a texture

  • Cream or lotion: the everyday choice. Some, like the Round Lab tube below, are sold as feeling like a moisturizer.
  • Stick: a solid balm you swipe on. Handy for reapplying on the go.
  • Cushion: sunscreen in a compact with a sponge.
  • Spray or mist: the MFDS says to spray it into your hand first, then apply, so it does not get into your eyes or mouth or get inhaled.
  • Mineral filters: look for zinc oxide in the ingredients. Round Lab, for one, sells a zinc oxide version called Mild-Up in the US.

Before you pay

  • Check both marks. SPF covers UVB and PA covers UVA, so look at both numbers, not just one.
  • Check water resistance if you are heading to the beach or a hike.
  • Check which version you hold. The same product can have a Korean and a US formula.

Best Everyday Moisturizing Sunscreen: Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen UVLock SPF 50 Broad Spectrum

Round Lab sells this as a daily sunscreen with a moisturizer-like feel, a soft dewy finish and no white cast. It pairs birch sap with hyaluronic acid for hydration. It is also easy to rebuy: the Korean version is on Round Lab's Korean store, and the US version is on its US store and its official Amazon listing.

Round Lab says more than 20 million have sold worldwide (brand figure on its US store, checked Nov. 16, 2026).

Who it suits: Normal to dry skin that likes a moisturizing finish, and anyone who wants one sunscreen they can rebuy at home. The US label says to use a water-resistant sunscreen if you swim or sweat, so bring a different one to the beach.

How to use: Apply liberally and evenly 15 minutes before sun exposure, and reapply at least every 2 hours, as the US Drug Facts direct. Use it as the last skincare step, before makeup.

Buying in Korea vs. the US

  • Same name, different box. The Korean tube is labeled SPF50+ PA++++. The US tube says SPF 50 Broad Spectrum and has a Drug Facts box. Round Lab has also filed a US label for an SPF 45 version, so read the tube you are holding.
  • Prices on official stores (Nov. 16, 2026): ₩25,000 on Round Lab's Korean store (₩22,500 on sale), and $28.00 on its US store ($17.49 on sale).
  • Back home: buy from Round Lab's US store or its official Amazon listing, not from resellers, so you get the US-labeled formula.

How to wear it so the number counts

  • Use enough. SPF is tested at 2 mg per square centimeter of skin, the MFDS says. Too little, and you may not get the protection on the label.
  • Put it on early. The MFDS suggests 15 minutes before you go out.
  • Reapply. The FDA says at least every two hours, and more often if you swim or sweat. The MFDS says even long-lasting water-resistant products need reapplying every two hours during long water play.
  • Wash it off. Cleanse at night so no sunscreen stays on your skin.
  • Stop if it stings. If you get a rash or irritation, stop using it and see a dermatologist.

Korean words on the box

  • 선크림 (seon-keu-rim): sunscreen cream.
  • 자외선 차단 (ja-oe-seon cha-dan): UV protection.
  • 기능성화장품 (gi-neung-seong hwa-jang-pum): functional cosmetic, the mark the MFDS tells shoppers to look for.
  • 내수성 (nae-su-seong): water resistant. 지속내수성 is the long-lasting version.

Not sure what you are holding? Show a staff member this page and point to the word.

item.title: Aestura vs Illiyoon: Which Korean Moisturizer to Buy
item.description: Aestura Atobarrier365 or Illiyoon Ceramide Ato? Texture, key ingredients, sizes and where to buy each, so you can pick the right cream for your skin.
item.content:encoded:
Pick Aestura Atobarrier365 Cream if you want a face cream in a small 80 ml tube that is easy to reorder on Amazon US. Pick Illiyoon Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream if you want a bigger fragrance-free, vegan cream that Amorepacific sells as body care.

Both creams come from Amorepacific, and both sit on the dry-and-sensitive shelf at Olive Young. They look alike on paper. In practice, they suit different jobs.

Aestura’s cream is a face cream in a small tube. Illiyoon’s comes in bigger tubes, and Amorepacific files it under body care. That one difference explains most of what follows.

The short version

  • Texture: the brand calls Aestura soft and non-sticky. It calls Illiyoon melting, with a smooth finish.
  • Key ingredient: Aestura lists ceramide NP, cholesterol and niacinamide. Illiyoon leads with a ceramide it calls CPP-40, plus madecassoside.
  • Size: Aestura comes in 80 ml. Illiyoon comes in 150 ml to 230 ml in Korea, and 6.76 fl. oz. on Amazon US.
  • Fragrance: both are fragrance-free, according to the brand pages. Illiyoon’s label also says vegan.
  • Where to buy: Olive Young in Seoul carries both. On Amazon US, each is sold by the brand’s own seller.

Pick Aestura if…

  • You want a cream for your face only.
  • You need a small tube that fits a carry-on bag.
  • You like niacinamide in a moisturizer.

Pick Illiyoon if…

  • You want one cream for face, arms and legs.
  • You share skincare with a partner or family.
  • You prefer a vegan, fragrance-free label.

What the labels actually say

Aestura’s tube reads “Moisturizing & strengthening skin barrier” and “For dry & sensitive skin.” Illiyoon’s reads “For Sensitive & Dry Skin,” “Fragrance Free,” “9 FREE” and “Vegan.”

Those are the brands’ words. Both are cosmetics, not treatments. If you have a skin condition, ask a dermatologist what to use.

Ingredients they share

Read the full lists and the two creams overlap more than you’d expect. Both contain ceramide NP, cholesterol, phytosphingosine, squalane, glycerin and mannitol.

The differences are in the extras. Aestura adds niacinamide and allantoin. Illiyoon adds madecassoside, black soybean oil, ginseng water and a few plant extracts.

If you react to plant extracts, note that Aestura’s list has none. If you avoid animal-derived ingredients, Illiyoon is the one labeled vegan.

Can you use both?

Yes. Following each brand’s directions, that means Aestura on your face morning and evening, and Illiyoon on your arms, legs and any dry spots on the body.

Reading the box in the store

Korean packaging mixes Korean and English. Three words help on the shelf:

  • 민감 (min-gam): sensitive
  • 건조 (geon-jo): dry
  • 무향 (mu-hyang): fragrance-free

Illiyoon’s front label prints 민감&건조 피부용, “for sensitive & dry skin,” next to the English.

Best for the Face: AESTURA Atobarrier365 Cream

A face cream made for dry and sensitive skin. The label says "moisturizing & strengthening skin barrier." The brand describes a soft, fragrance-free texture that sits on skin without feeling sticky. The 80 ml tube is small enough for a carry-on.

Who it suits: Dry or sensitive skin that wants one cream for the face, and anyone who wants to reorder it on Amazon at home.

How to use: The brand says to use it morning and evening: spread an even layer over your face and let it sink in.

Best Big-Tube Cream: ILLIYOON Ceramide Ato Concentrate Cream

Amorepacific lists this cream under body care on its own store. The label reads fragrance free, vegan and "9 FREE," with soy-ceramide and madecassoside up front. The brand calls the texture melting, with a smooth finish. It comes in tubs big enough to share.

Who it suits: Dry, sensitive skin, households that share one cream, and anyone who avoids added fragrance.

How to use: The brand says to apply a generous amount to dry areas such as the face, arms and legs, and to reapply often on very dry spots.

How to use a barrier cream in your routine

  • Last step at night: cleanser, then toner or serum if you use them, then the cream.
  • In the morning: cream first, then sunscreen on top.
  • On the body: Illiyoon suggests its Ceramide Ato Lotion first and the cream on spots that stay dry.
  • Amount: cover the area in a thin, even layer. Add more on dry patches rather than over the whole face.

Buying in Seoul vs the US

In Seoul: Olive Young carries both creams, sometimes as sets with minis. On November 16, 2026, Amorepacific's own mall listed Aestura's 80 ml at ₩33,000 and Illiyoon's 230 ml at ₩21,900 before discounts.

In the US: buy from the brand's own Amazon seller. Check that the listing says "Sold by AESTURA Official" or "Sold by ILLIYOON US." If a different seller name shows up, look again before you buy.

Sizes differ by market. Illiyoon comes in 150 ml at Olive Young, 230 ml on Amorepacific's mall and 6.76 fl. oz. on Amazon US. Compare the price per ml, not the price per tub.

Patch test first

The American Academy of Dermatology suggests testing a new product before you add it to your routine. Apply it to a quarter-sized spot, such as the inside of your elbow, twice a day for 7 to 10 days.

If your skin reacts, stop using it. If irritation keeps coming back, a dermatologist can do a patch test to find the cause.

item.title: Korean Scalp Care: Scrubs, Tonics and Brushes Visitors Buy
item.description: Korean scalp care is a visitor favorite at Olive Young. What scalp scrubs, tonics, ampoules and brushes do, how to use each, and what labels mean.
item.content:encoded:
Korean scalp care treats your scalp like skin: a scrub to clear buildup, a leave-on tonic or ampoule for a cool, refreshed feel, and a brush to massage it in. At Olive Young, hair tonics and ampoules are a visitor favorite, with foreign shoppers making up 28% of their sales.

Scalp care is a rising trend among visitors at Olive Young. Foreign shoppers made up 28% of the chain’s sales of hair tonics and ampoules from January to August 2026, Olive Young said, above the roughly 18% they made up across hair care overall.

The draw is the format. Olive Young singled out roll-on and brush-tip scalp products from brands such as LABO-H and Lilyeve, which are easy to use and easy to pack.

What Korean scalp care is

The idea is simple: treat your scalp like the skin on your face. Cleanse it well, clear buildup, and keep it comfortable.

  • Scalp scrub: a rinse-off product with salt or other grains that clears buildup from styling products and oil.
  • Scaling shampoo: a deep-cleansing shampoo, often labeled 스케일링 (scaling).
  • Tonic or ampoule: a leave-on liquid you apply straight to the scalp, often with menthol for a cooling feel.
  • Scalp brush: a handheld brush, usually silicone, to massage shampoo or scrub across the scalp.

Who it suits

  • Oily scalp, frequent styling: a weekly scrub or scaling shampoo.
  • A scalp that feels hot or tight: a cooling leave-on tonic.
  • Long or thick hair: brush-tip ampoules reach the scalp without soaking your hair.
  • Sensitive scalp: go easy on scrubs, and try a product on a small area first.

How to use a scalp scrub

Aromatica’s directions for its Rosemary Scalp Scrub are a good template:

  • Wet hair and scalp well with lukewarm water.
  • Apply section by section, using the pointed tip along your parts.
  • Massage gently with your fingertips.
  • Add a little water, work up a lather, then rinse thoroughly.
  • Two to three times a week, in place of shampoo or before it.

How to use a tonic or ampoule

  • Start with a clean scalp, towel-dried.
  • Apply directly to the scalp, not the lengths. Brush and roll-on tips make this easy.
  • Massage it in. Do not rinse. LABO-H’s directions say to use its ampoule daily or as often as you like.

A word on hair loss

Many Korean scalp products carry hair-loss wording on the box. Treat them as scalp care. If you are losing hair, see a dermatologist.

Where to shop in Seoul

  • Olive Young: 151 of its stores sat in what it calls global tourist districts as of August 2026, with staff who speak foreign languages and signs in several languages.
  • Ask in your language: since June 2026, some Seoul Olive Young stores have an AI shopping assistant that answers by voice in eight languages, including English.
  • Shop more than one store: foreign shoppers surveyed in its tourist-district stores in May 2026 said they visited 2.8 stores on average. Lineups and sales differ by store.

Pack it right

  • Tonics and ampoules are liquids. Small bottles can go in your carry-on liquids bag if they meet the size limit; big bottles go in checked luggage.
  • Lock the tip. LABO-H’s ampoule twists to OPEN and CLOSE. Close it before you pack.

Products to look for

  • Scalp scrub: Aromatica Rosemary Scalp Scrub, 165 g. Aromatica describes it as an Andes lake salt scrub with rosemary and a precision tip that glides along your part to clear old buildup.
  • Brush-tip ampoules: LABO-H and Lilyeve. Olive Young named both brands as drawing attention from visitors with roll-on and brush-type scalp products (CJ, Aug. 2026). LABO-H is an Amorepacific brand.
  • A scalp massage brush: Aromatica suggests pairing its scrub with one to work the salt across your scalp.

Product names and lineups change often in Korea. Show a photo to Olive Young staff if you cannot find the exact one.

What the labels mean

  • 두피 (du-pi): scalp.
  • 스케일링 (seu-ke-il-ling): scaling, a deep-cleansing scalp product.
  • 토닉 / 앰플: tonic / ampoule, both leave-on.
  • 탈모 증상 완화 (tal-mo jeung-sang wan-hwa): easing hair-loss symptoms. Korea's MFDS lists "products aiding in alleviating hair loss symptoms" as a functional cosmetic category. It is a cosmetic label, not a medicine, and not a promise.
  • 쿨링 (ku-ling): cooling, usually from menthol.

When to skip the shelf

  • Sudden or patchy hair loss: see a board-certified dermatologist. The American Academy of Dermatology says finding the cause comes first.
  • A sore, red or flaking scalp: ask a dermatologist before scrubbing. Aromatica's own directions say not to use its scrub on broken or irritated skin.
  • Medicated products: some pharmacy scalp products in Korea are medicines. Ask the pharmacist before buying them.

item.title: Myeongdong Beauty Shopping Route: A Half-Day Plan
item.description: A simple Myeongdong beauty shopping route: the subway stop, Daiso's 12 floors, Olive Young's biggest Myeongdong store, brand shops, and tax refund tips.
item.content:encoded:
Take Seoul Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station, start at Daiso's multi-floor Myeongdong Station store, then walk into the main streets for Olive Young's large Central Myeongdong Town store, brand shops and pharmacies. Bring your passport for tax refunds, and expect company: Myeongdong drew about 4.5 million foreign visitors in the first half of 2025.

Myeongdong is where most visitors to Seoul end up, and for good reason. In the first half of 2025, about 4.55 million foreign visitors went to Myeongdong, the most of any area in Korea for the second year running, according to LG U+ roaming data reported by Maeil Business. Korea.net, the government news service, called it the starting point of K-beauty.

The streets are packed with beauty stores, so a plan helps. Here is a simple order that works in half a day.

Getting there

  • Subway: Seoul Subway Line 4, Myeongdong Station. Visit Seoul lists Exits 5 to 10 for the shopping streets.
  • Hours: the area is open daily, but hours vary by store, Visit Seoul says.
  • Map tip: search each store by name in a map app. Many chains have more than one branch here.

What you’ll find

  • Olive Young: eight stores in Myeongdong, Newstop reported in October 2026. The biggest is Central Myeongdong Town, opened in March 2026: three floors, about 1,000 brands and 15,000 products, Cosinkorea reported.
  • Daiso: two Myeongdong stores. The Myeongdong Station store reopened in 2023 in a building of 12 floors, with beauty on the 2nd floor and snacks on the 5th, Businesspost reported.
  • Brand stores: single-brand cosmetics shops line the streets. Visit Seoul lists an Etude House store about 50 m from its Myeongdong map point.
  • Pharmacies: many sell skincare to visitors. Read our pharmacy guide before you buy anything that could be medicine.

A sample route

  1. Daiso Myeongdong Station store. It sits across a main road from the heart of Myeongdong. Many shoppers ride the elevator to the top floor and walk down, Businesspost observed. Stock up on low-cost basics here first.
  2. Cross into the main streets. Head for Olive Young Central Myeongdong Town. Its “Mask Library” holds about 800 sheet masks and other masks, sorted by skin type and function, Cosinkorea reported.
  3. Brand stores and pharmacies. Now you know Olive Young’s prices, so compare before you pay twice for the same thing.
  4. Lunch break. Visit Seoul lists Myeongdong Kyoja, a kal-guksu (knife-cut noodle soup) restaurant, about 50 m from its Myeongdong map point.
  5. One last stop. Go back for anything you skipped, then head home before your bags get too heavy.

Before you go

  • Make a short list. Thousands of products in one store is a lot. Our first Olive Young list helps.
  • Ask for help in English. At Central Myeongdong Town, staff who speak English, Chinese or Japanese wear flag badges, Cosinkorea reported.
  • Save receipts. Keep tax refund receipts together for the airport.
  • Leave room in your bag. Masks and tubes add up fast, and Daiso and Olive Young are only the start of the walk.

Tax-free tips for this route

  • Passport in your pocket, not in the hotel safe. Stores check it at the register.
  • Buy in bigger baskets. A refund needs ₩15,000 or more per purchase, and an immediate refund at the register works for payments under ₩1,000,000 (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).
  • Keep it sealed. Refunded items must stay unopened until you leave Korea (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).

Full steps, airport counters and how much you get back are in our tax refund guide.

Beat the crowds

  • Know the peak. Visit Seoul says Myeongdong fills with Japanese and Chinese tourists during Golden Week, the spring holiday period in both countries.
  • Big stores move faster. Olive Young's Central Myeongdong Town runs 22 staffed checkout counters for large orders, Cosinkorea reported.
  • Use the floor guide at Daiso. The Myeongdong Station store keeps one by the first-floor elevator in Korean, English, Japanese and Chinese, Businesspost reported in 2023.
  • Check hours first. Visit Seoul lists the area as open daily, with hours that vary by store.

Keep walking: Euljiro and Gwangjang Market

Myeongdong does not have to be the end of the day. Korea.net reported in December 2025 that visitors increasingly link Myeongdong with nearby Euljiro and Gwangjang Market into one route.

  • Euljiro: old printing-shop alleys with cafes and bars, popular with younger visitors.
  • Gwangjang Market: a traditional market known for street food.

The roaming data backs it up. Maeil Business reported that areas next to Myeongdong, such as Gwanghui-dong, Pil-dong and Euljiro-dong, gained close to 400,000 foreign visitors each on average in the first half of 2025, compared with a year earlier.

item.title: Korean Dry Skin Routine: 3 Steps, Morning and Night
item.description: A three-step Korean routine for dry skin: a watery toner, a rich ceramide cream and sunscreen. What to use, how much, in what order, and where to buy it.
item.content:encoded:
In the morning, pat on a watery toner, smooth on a rich cream while your skin is still damp, and finish with sunscreen. At night, cleanse gently and repeat the toner and cream without sunscreen, and add more cream whenever your skin feels tight.

Dry skin feels tight after washing and flaky by afternoon. You don’t need ten steps for that. Three products in the morning and two at night cover the basics.

The idea is simple. Put water on first with a thin toner. Then hold it in with a rich cream. In the morning, add sunscreen on top.

Why thin first, then rich

  • Toner adds water. It is watery, so it goes on first and spreads easily over clean skin.
  • Cream keeps it there. The American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) says creams and ointments add more moisture than lotions.
  • Timing matters. The AAD suggests applying moisturizer while your skin is still damp. So go from toner to cream without waiting.
  • Sunscreen goes last. The AAD recommends a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher for dry skin, too.

AESTURA, the brand of the cream below, prints the same order in its directions: after toner and serum.

The routine at a glance

  • Morning: VT PDRN Glow Toner, then AESTURA Atobarrier365 Cream, then Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen.
  • Night: a gentle cleanser, the toner, then the cream.
  • During the day: more cream on any spot that feels tight. The AAD suggests moisturizing several times a day.

One thing to know first

The AAD suggests fragrance-free products for dry skin. The VT toner lists fragrance, and AESTURA says its cream has less than 1%. If your skin stings, switch to a fragrance-free toner and keep the rest.

Step 1, Toner: VT PDRN Glow Toner

A milky, watery toner that costs ₩5,000 for 200 ml at Daiso. It gives dry skin a first layer of water before the cream goes on. The label lists glycerin, niacinamide and sodium hyaluronate near the top.

Who it suits: Anyone in Seoul who wants a cheap first step. Skip it if fragrance bothers your skin: fragrance is on the ingredient list.

How to use: After cleansing, put some on a cotton pad or your palms. Spread it from the center of your face outward. Go straight to the cream while your skin is still damp.

Step 2, Moisturizer: AESTURA Atobarrier365 Cream

This is the rich step. It is a thick cream with ceramides, cholesterol and fatty acids, plus squalane and glycerin. AESTURA tells you to use it morning and night, after toner and serum.

Who it suits: Skin that feels tight by midday or flakes around the nose and cheeks. It is not fully fragrance-free: the brand says it contains less than 1% synthetic fragrance.

How to use: Morning and night, after the toner. Smooth an even layer over your face, then press it in with your palms. You can see small capsules in the cream; they melt as you spread it.

Step 3, Sunscreen: Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen UVLock SPF 50

A lotion-like sunscreen, so it doesn't undo the moisture you just added. The US version is labeled SPF 50 Broad Spectrum. Besides the sunscreen filters, it has birch sap, glycerin and hyaluronic acid.

Who it suits: Anyone who skips sunscreen because it feels drying or leaves a white film. Check the label if you buy it in Korea: the Korean and US versions can be labeled differently.

How to use: Last step of the morning, over the cream. Apply generously and evenly 15 minutes before you go out. Reapply at least every 2 hours outdoors, as the label says.

The night version

  • Cleanse gently: use a mild cleanser and only enough to remove dirt and oil. The AAD warns against a thick lather on dry skin.
  • Toner, then cream: same two steps as the morning. Put the cream on while your face is still damp.
  • No sunscreen: you only need it for daytime.
  • Humidifier: the AAD suggests running one in your bedroom while you sleep.

Common mistakes with dry skin

  • Long, hot showers: the AAD suggests 5 to 10 minutes in warm water, then patting skin dry.
  • Lotion instead of cream: the AAD says creams and ointments add more moisture than lotions.
  • Waiting too long: apply moisturizer while skin is still damp after washing.
  • Stinging products: the AAD lists alcohol, fragrance and retinoids as things to stop if your skin is dry. If anything burns or stings, stop and ask a dermatologist.

Where to buy

In Seoul: the VT toner is a Daiso product. Daiso Mall listed it at ₩5,000 on Nov. 16, 2026.

In the US: the AESTURA cream and Round Lab sunscreen are on Amazon from the brands' own stores (checked Nov. 16, 2026). Round Lab also sells the sunscreen on its US site.

item.title: Korea Tax Refund on Beauty Shopping: How It Works
item.description: How visitors get tax back on Korean beauty shopping: the ₩15,000 minimum, immediate refunds at the register, airport kiosks and what to bring.
item.content:encoded:
In Korea you can get tax back on purchases of ₩15,000 or more at stores with a Tax Refund sign, either taken off at the register or claimed before you fly (as of Nov. 16, 2026, per VisitKorea). Show your passport when you pay, keep items unopened, and get customs approval at the airport if the store didn't refund you.

Korea’s price tags include tax. As a visitor you can get part of it back, and cosmetics and perfume are on the list of eligible goods. Olive Young counts the nationalities of its foreign shoppers using Global Tax Free refund data: 192 countries in 2026, according to its Aug. 31 press release.

There are two ways to get the money. One takes the tax off at the register. The other refunds it later, in the city or at the airport.

Who qualifies

  • Visitors: foreigners staying in Korea for less than six months (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).
  • Overseas Koreans: staying less than three months and living abroad for two years or more, or holding permanent residency elsewhere (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).
  • Your items: new, unopened and unused, taken out of Korea within three months of purchase (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).

The numbers to know

  • Minimum: ₩15,000 per purchase at a participating store (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).
  • Immediate refund at the register: each payment must be under ₩1,000,000, and your total for the trip can’t go over ₩5,000,000 (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).
  • Downtown refund booths: up to ₩6,000,000 per receipt (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).
  • Airport refund counters: no limit on the purchase amount (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).

Rules do change. The immediate refund limits doubled on Jan. 1, 2024, from ₩500,000 per purchase and ₩2,500,000 in total, according to the Korean government’s Korea.net news service. Check the counter if a number looks different.

Option 1: Immediate refund at the store

  • Look for the sign. Stores show “Tax Refund” or “Tax Free” with a refund company’s logo.
  • Hand over your passport before you pay and say you want a tax refund.
  • Pay the lower price. The tax comes off on the spot.
  • Nothing to do at the airport for these purchases. VisitKorea lists departure as the last step.

Option 2: Refund later

  • Get a tax refund receipt. A regular receipt won’t work.
  • Downtown: claim at a city refund booth or kiosk with your passport, receipt and a credit card. You still show the items to customs when you leave.
  • Airport: get the customs stamp, then claim at a counter or kiosk.
  • Mobile: some refund companies let you apply through their app or site after customs approval.

What to bring

  • Passport: the original, every time you shop.
  • Receipts: keep tax refund receipts flat in one envelope.
  • Unopened items: pack refunded items where you can reach them at customs.
  • A credit card: downtown booths ask for one.
  • Extra time: give yourself a buffer at the airport if you still need the customs stamp. Customs comes before bag drop, not after.

At the airport, step by step

Skip this if every purchase was refunded at the register. For the rest, VisitKorea lists this order:

  • Check in first, but don't drop your bag yet. Keep refund receipts and the items with you.
  • Go to customs. Show the items, receipts and passport to get the export approval stamp.
  • Then check your bag at the oversized baggage counter.
  • Claim the refund at a refund counter or kiosk. At Incheon, cash is paid in the duty-free zone after security.

Incheon Terminal 1: the refund counter is near Gate 28 on the 3rd floor. Staffed hours are 07:00 to 22:00, and kiosks run 24 hours (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea tax refund guide). Locations change, so check the signs when you arrive.

How much you actually get back

  • About 5 to 8% of the purchase price, after the refund company's processing fee (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea tax refund guide).
  • Method matters. Refunds to a credit card or mobile payment carry separate fees, so you get a little less (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea tax refund guide).
  • Mailbox refunds take time. If the counter is closed, you fill in the receipt and drop it in the box. The refund reaches your card in 1 to 2 months (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: VisitKorea).

Say it at the register

  • "택스 리펀 돼요?" (taek-seu ri-peon dwae-yo?) Can I get a tax refund?
  • "즉시 환급 돼요?" (jeuk-si hwan-geup dwae-yo?) Can you take it off now?
  • "여권 여기 있어요." (yeo-gwon yeo-gi i-sseo-yo.) Here's my passport.

Say it before the cashier rings you up. It is easier than fixing a receipt afterward.

item.title: Korean Lip Tint Guide: Finishes, Gradient Lips, Removal
item.description: How to choose a Korean lip tint: water, gloss and velvet finishes, how to do a gradient lip, why tints stain, how to take them off, and picks from Seoul.
item.content:encoded:
A Korean lip tint is a liquid lip color that leaves a stain, so the color stays after the shine fades. Choose a water or gloss tint for a juicy look, a velvet or blur tint for a soft matte look, and dab it on the center of your lips for a gradient.

Lip tint is one of the easiest Korean makeup buys to try. It is small, light to pack and often costs less than a lipstick.

A tint is not the same as a lipstick or gloss. It leaves a stain, so color stays after the shine wears off. That is why tints suit long days of walking and eating in Seoul.

Three finishes to know

  • Water tint: thin and watery. Daiso sells water tints like the Bonsep Water Veil Tint for ₩3,000.
  • Gloss or glass tint: shiny like a gloss, with a stain underneath. rom&nd describes its Juicy Lasting Tint as a lightweight gloss with a thick, glass-like shine and intense pigment.
  • Velvet or blur tint: soft and matte. Daiso Mall’s lip filters list velvet, blur and matte next to glow and water, so you’ll see these words on labels.

Who should buy what

  • First tint ever: a water tint. It is the easiest to blend and forgiving if you go too far.
  • Glossy, juicy look: a gloss tint like rom&nd’s.
  • Soft, grown-up look: a velvet or blur tint.
  • Only shine, no stain: a gloss, like the ₩5,000 Prelude Dinto La Belle Rose Glass Lip Gloss at Daiso.

The gradient lip

The gradient lip is the Korean look you see most: deeper color in the center, fading toward the edges. rom&nd’s own directions match it. Start from the center of your lips, spread the color outward as much as you like and add another layer for more color.

The trick is to stop before the outer line. Blend the edges with a fingertip so the color looks like it comes from inside the lip.

Popular tints on Seoul shelves

These were in Olive Young Korea’s makeup sales ranking on Nov. 16, 2026. Prices are list prices, and many were on sale for less.

  • Dinto Blur Jelly Plumping Lip Tint (#3), from ₩20,000. Ten shades. The highest-ranked lip tint on the list.
  • Tony Moly Get It Tint Waterful Syrup (#15), ₩16,000. A 5.3 g tint, on sale from Nov. 1 to 28, 2026.
  • rom&nd The Juicy Lasting Tint (#19), ₩13,000. rom&nd’s US store sells its Juicy Lasting Tint for $14, so you can find it again at home.

On a budget

Daiso’s lip shelf runs from ₩1,000 to ₩5,000. Pair a ₩3,000 Bonsep Water Veil Tint with a ₩1,000 Stylish Auto Lip Liner Pencil to test the look. Our budget makeup guide has more.

About staining

Staining is the point of a tint, but it also means color can stay on your lips into the evening. rom&nd says the color of its Juicy Lasting Tint stays true and deepens over time. Remove it with an oil-based cleanser or a lip and eye remover at night.

How to wear a tint, step by step

  • Prep your lips. Tints can look patchy on dry lips. Put on a thin balm, wait a few minutes, then blot it off.
  • Dab the center. One dot on the inner top lip and one on the inner bottom lip.
  • Blend outward. Press your lips together, then tap the edges with a fingertip.
  • Build if you want. Add a second layer in the center for a deeper gradient, or cover your whole lip for a bold look.
  • Add shine last. A clear gloss on top brings back the juicy look once the tint has set.

Before you buy

Swatch on your hand, then wait. rom&nd says the color of its tint deepens over time, so check the swatch after a few minutes.

Read the finish word. On Korean labels, 워터 (water), 글로우 (glow) and 글로스 (gloss) look shiny. 벨벳 (velvet), 블러 (blur) and 매트 (matte) look soft.

Pick by your undertone. Some rom&nd US pages list a color type for each shade, like "Soft Summer." If you know your seasonal color, use it as a shortcut.

Tints and dry lips

  • Watery and gloss tints often feel lighter. rom&nd calls its Juicy Lasting Tint hydrating and comfortable on lips.
  • Velvet and blur tints look softer but can show dry patches. Balm first.
  • Take it off at night. Remove the stain, then put on balm before bed. A ₩1,000 tinted balm from Daiso works for this.

item.title: Daiso Korea Beauty Finds: 4 Picks Under ₩5,000
item.description: The sheet masks and toner visitors buy most at Daiso in Seoul, what each one costs, who it suits, and how to pack them for the flight home.
item.content:encoded:
At Daiso Korea, start with the VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask and the two Vaseline sheet masks, ₩1,000 each, which were the top three beauty buys for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong. Add the ₩5,000 VT PDRN Glow Toner, Daiso Mall's best seller in early 2026.

Daiso is Korea’s fixed-price store, and nothing on its shelves costs more than ₩5,000. For many visitors, the beauty aisle is where the basket fills up.

Visitor spending is climbing. Daiso told Hankyung that card spending by foreign visitors rose 60% in 2025, then another 70% in January to March 2026. At the Myeongdong store, sheet masks led the beauty sales.

What’s on this list

  • Top sheet mask: VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask, ₩1,000
  • Top toner: VT PDRN Glow Toner, ₩5,000
  • Richer mask: Vaseline Sheet Mask, Moisturizing, ₩1,000
  • Lighter mask: Vaseline Sheet Mask, Hydrating, ₩1,000

All four come to ₩8,000. Prices are from Daiso Mall, checked in November 2026.

Best Sheet Mask: VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask

A thick sheet that turns plump and jelly-like as it soaks up a watery essence. At ₩1,000 you can buy one for every night of your trip.

#1 beauty buy for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong (Daiso data reported by Hankyung, Apr. 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants an easy, low-cost hydrating mask. Daiso lists it for all skin types.

How to use: After cleansing, leave it on for 10 to 20 minutes. Peel it off and pat in the leftover essence. No rinsing.

Best Toner: VT PDRN Glow Toner

A 200 ml bottle of milky, watery toner for ₩5,000, the top price at Daiso. It has the same PDRN ingredient as the mask, so the two pair easily.

Best seller on Daiso Mall, Jan. 1 to June 21, 2026 (Daiso data reported by Herald Business, July 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who goes through toner fast and wants a big bottle for little money. Listed for all skin types.

How to use: After cleansing, put some on a cotton pad or your palms and smooth it from the center of your face outward. VT also suggests pouring it into a mist bottle.

Best Value Mask: Vaseline Sheet Mask, Moisturizing

A Daiso Korea sheet mask from a name every American knows. The essence is cream-type, with ceramide NP and a little petrolatum, so it feels richer than the hydrating one.

#2 beauty buy for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong (Daiso data reported by Hankyung, Apr. 2026).

Who it suits: Skin that feels dry or tight and wants a creamier mask.

How to use: On clean skin, smooth it over your eyes, nose and mouth and leave it on about 10 minutes. Remove it and pat in what's left.

Best for Hydration: Vaseline Sheet Mask, Hydrating

The lighter of the two Vaseline masks. Its ampoule-type essence carries hyaluronic acid, on the same eucalyptus-fiber sheet.

#3 beauty buy for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong (Daiso data reported by Hankyung, Apr. 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants water more than richness, or a lighter mask for a warm day.

How to use: Same as the moisturizing one: about 10 minutes on clean skin, then pat in the rest.

How to shop Daiso in Seoul

Prices are fixed. Nothing at Daiso costs more than ₩5,000, and there are about 1,500 stores in Korea, so one is rarely far away.

  • Check stock first: the Daiso Mall app shows which stores have an item and offers store pickup.
  • Myeongdong: Hankyung calls it the Daiso store where visitor buying shows most clearly, and masks lead its beauty sales.
  • Buy when you see it: the VT toner sold out widely after launch (Herald Business), so don't save it for your last day.

Tax-free at Daiso

Bring your physical passport. Tax-free shopping starts at ₩15,000 in one payment. (Amounts as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: Trip.com Korea Tax Refund Guide 2026. Rules can change, so check at the counter.) Daiso is among the stores with a Tax Free logo, where the tax can come off right at the register.

All four picks here add up to ₩8,000. To reach ₩15,000, put everything in one basket and pay once.

Packing for the flight home

  • Carry-on (US flights): liquids and gels must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less per container, all in one quart-size bag.
  • Toner: the 200 ml bottle is over the limit. It goes in your checked bag.
  • Masks: each pouch holds 23 to 25 ml, under the limit, but a stack fills your quart bag fast. Lay them flat in your checked bag instead.

item.title: Seoul Hair Salon Guide: Booking, Prices, Tipping
item.description: Before a Seoul hair salon visit: how to book on Naver Map, how length surcharges work, the perm and color words to know, what to bring, and why you don't tip.
item.content:encoded:
Book a Seoul hair salon ahead, usually on Naver Map, and bring three to five reference photos. Expect the posted price to rise with hair length and add-ons, ask for the total before the stylist starts, and skip the tip, because tipping is not customary in Korea.

Korea has a lot of salons. KB Financial Group’s research institute counted more than 110,000 hair salons and barbershops in September 2020, or 21.3 per 10,000 people, the Korea Herald reported. The US figure was about two.

That means choice, and a few local habits worth knowing before you book. Here is how booking, pricing and tipping work.

Three kinds of shop

  • Miyongsil (미용실): the everyday salon for all ages and genders. Go here for perms, color and longer cuts.
  • Ibalso (이발소): the traditional barbershop, mostly for older men, with shaving.
  • Barbershop: short cuts, usually for younger men.

Booking

  • Use Naver. Most salons, including big chains, take reservations mostly through Naver, the Korea Herald says. Weekend walk-ins are often impossible.
  • No Korean phone number? Since June 2026, Naver lets travelers with a foreign passport verify on their phone for reservations, orders and payments, the Korea Times reported.
  • Message first if your hair needs it. If you have curly hair, send a photo through the salon’s social media and ask whether a stylist has experience with it.

How the price works

  • Posted price is a starting point. Price ranges are usually shown outside the shop. Compare a few.
  • Length adds up. Many salons add a length surcharge on top of the base fee for perms and color. Some use bands like jawline, shoulder, collarbone and mid-back. The surcharge can even exceed the main service.
  • Add-ons are optional. Stylists often suggest treatments or products. Declining is fine.
  • Ask for the total. When you get three or more services, salons must disclose each price and the total before they start (reported Apr. 2024; checked Nov. 16, 2026. Source: Korea Herald). For one or two services, ask anyway.

What to bring

  • Reference photos. Three to five images from the front, side and back.
  • A translation app for anything the photos don’t cover.
  • Your passport and a card, the basics visitor guides list.

How long to block out

  • Perm: about 3 hours, Creatrip says.
  • Color without bleach: about 3 hours.
  • Color with bleach: 3 to 5 hours. Plan nothing tight after.
  • Extras: upscale salons often include a head massage, shampoo, snacks and drinks, the Korea Herald notes. Ask what is included when you book.

Tipping

  • Don’t tip. Tipping is not customary in Korea. Mandatory service fees or built-in tips go against Korean rules, while a voluntary tip is legal (as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: Korea Times). A warm thank-you is the norm.

Words to show your stylist

  • 커트 (keo-teu): haircut.
  • 펌 (peom): perm. Korean perms default to waves, the Korea Herald notes, so ask for a straight perm by name if that is what you want.
  • 다운펌 (da-un-peom): down perm, a popular option for short hair.
  • 셋팅펌 (set-ting-peom): setting perm, a common Korean perm style.
  • 염색 (yeom-saek): hair color.
  • 탈색 (tal-saek): bleach. It adds hours to the appointment.
  • 클리닉 (keul-li-nik): hair treatment. Fine to decline.
  • 기장 추가 (gi-jang chu-ga): length surcharge.

Phrases for the chair

  • "총 얼마예요?" (chong eol-ma-ye-yo?) What is the total?
  • "기장 추가 있어요?" (gi-jang chu-ga i-sseo-yo?) Is there a length charge?
  • "이 사진처럼 해 주세요." (i sa-jin-cheo-reom hae ju-se-yo) Like this photo, please.
  • "괜찮아요." (gwaen-chan-a-yo) No thanks. Use it for add-ons you don't want.

If a stylist asks whether you have plans after this, the Korea Herald explains, saying yes signals you don't need styling or a blow-dry. Say no if you want it.

Before you sit down

  • Screenshot your photos. Salon Wi-Fi can be slow, so save images to your phone.
  • Tell your hair history. Mention bleach, perms or straightening from the past six months.
  • Space chemical services. Creatrip recommends at least 15 days between a perm and a color.
  • Bring a card and your passport. Visitor guides list both as the basics.
  • Cancel early. Give at least 24 hours' notice to avoid a cancellation fee.

item.title: What Is PDRN in Skin Care? Salmon DNA and Plant PDRN
item.description: PDRN in Korean skin care, explained: what the label calls it, salmon versus plant sources, how creams differ from clinic injections, and three picks.
item.content:encoded:
In Korean skin care, PDRN usually shows up on the ingredient list as sodium DNA, taken from salmon or, in some newer products, made with plant extracts like ginseng. In a toner or cream it works as a skin-conditioning ingredient for hydration and glow, which is different from the PDRN injections done in clinics.

PDRN is on Korean beauty shelves everywhere this year, from ₩1,000 sheet masks at Daiso to brand-name creams. You will also hear it called “salmon DNA.”

The name sounds clinical, and Seoul skin clinics do use PDRN in injections. The bottle on the shelf is a different product. Here is what PDRN means on a cosmetic label, where it comes from, and how to choose.

PDRN in one minute

  • The name: PDRN stands for polydeoxyribonucleotide. It refers to DNA fragments, traditionally purified from salmon or trout.
  • On the label: in cosmetics it usually appears as sodium DNA. Cosmetics Europe’s COSMILE database lists it as a skin-conditioning ingredient.
  • Salmon or plant: some brands use salmon-derived DNA. Others, like VT’s Daiso line, make a version with plant extracts such as ginseng.
  • What to expect: hydration and a glowy look, mostly thanks to the moisturizing ingredients around it.

Salmon PDRN vs. plant PDRN

  • Salmon: Anua says the PDRN in its moisturizing cream is derived from salmon DNA.
  • Plant: VT calls its version VT Panax PDRN. On Daiso Mall, VT lists it as water, wild-cultivated ginseng extract, 1,2-hexanediol and sodium DNA.
  • If you avoid animal ingredients: the word “plant” or “vegan” on the box is your best clue. When the source is not printed, ask the brand.

Why everyone is buying it

  • Low prices: at Daiso, a VT PDRN sheet mask costs ₩1,000. It was the top beauty buy for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong, Daiso data showed in April 2026.
  • Easy formats: toners, masks and creams fit into any routine you already have.
  • The clinic connection: the ingredient is known from skin-booster injections, which gives it a medical-sounding halo. That halo does not transfer to the cream.

Who should try it

  • Try it: if you like hydrating toners and masks and want to see the trend for yourself.
  • Skip the salmon version: if you avoid animal-derived ingredients.
  • Go slow: if your skin reacts to fragrance. Both VT products below contain it.

Three PDRN picks, from a one-night test to a daily cream:

Best Low-Cost Way to Try It: VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask

One sheet costs ₩1,000 at Daiso, so you can see how you like a PDRN product before you spend more. It is a thick jelly-like sheet soaked in a watery essence. VT uses its plant-based PDRN, made with wild-cultivated ginseng extract, in this line.

The top beauty buy for visitors at Daiso Myeongdong (Daiso data reported by Hankyung, Apr. 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone curious about PDRN who wants a cheap, one-night test. Skip it if fragrance bothers your skin.

How to use: After cleansing, smooth the sheet over your face and rest for 10 to 20 minutes. Peel it off and pat in what is left. No rinsing.

Best Big Bottle: VT PDRN Glow Toner

A milky, watery toner in a 200 ml bottle for ₩5,000. It uses the same ginseng-based PDRN ingredient as the mask, so the two go together. The label puts glycerin, niacinamide and sodium hyaluronate to work alongside it for hydration.

Best seller on Daiso Mall, Jan. 1 to June 21, 2026 (Daiso data reported by Herald Business, July 2026).

Who it suits: People who go through toner fast and want a big bottle for little money. Daiso lists it for all skin types.

How to use: After cleansing, pour some onto a cotton pad or your palms and spread it from the center of your face outward. VT also suggests putting it in a mist bottle.

Best Salmon-Derived Pick: Anua PDRN Hyaluronic Acid 100 Moisturizing Cream

If you want the salmon version, Anua says the PDRN in this cream is derived from salmon DNA. It is a daily moisturizer that pairs sodium DNA with several forms of hyaluronic acid for hydration and a natural-looking glow.

Who it suits: People who want a moisturizer rather than a toner, and who do not mind an animal-derived ingredient.

How to use: Anua suggests it morning and night as the last step of your skincare routine. In the morning, sunscreen goes on after it.

How to read a PDRN label

  • Look for sodium DNA. That is the usual ingredient-list name. The word PDRN on the front is a marketing name.
  • Check how far down it sits. Ingredients are listed from most to least. In both VT products, sodium DNA sits near the end.
  • Notice tiny numbers. VT prints the amount next to the ingredient: 5 ppb in the toner and 250 ppb in the mask. Parts per billion are very small amounts.
  • Find the source. Anua says salmon. VT says ginseng. If the box says neither, the label alone may not tell you.
  • Read the rest of the list. Glycerin, hyaluronic acid and niacinamide do much of the hydrating work in these formulas.

Creams vs. clinic injections

Two very different things share one name. Korean skin clinics offer PDRN and polynucleotide injections as a medical procedure. A toner or cream is a cosmetic you use at home.

The US rules differ too. Injectable PDRN is not FDA-approved for cosmetic use, Dermatology Times reports. Topical PDRN is sold in the US as a cosmetic.

Our take: buy PDRN skincare for hydration and glow, and judge it the way you would any moisturizer. If you are thinking about a clinic procedure in Seoul, talk to a dermatologist first, ideally one you can follow up with at home.

Where to buy in Seoul

  • Daiso: the VT PDRN Glow line, at ₩1,000 for the mask and ₩5,000 for the toner on Daiso Mall.
  • Anua at home: the cream is on Anua's official US store, so you can reorder after the trip.
  • Patch test first: both VT items contain fragrance. Try a new product on a small area before using it on your whole face.

item.title: Korean Beauty Gifts to Bring Home from Seoul
item.description: The Korean beauty gifts worth packing: who each one suits, how to fit them in a carry-on, and where in Seoul to buy them without overspending.
item.content:encoded:
Bring perfume hand creams, single sheet masks and boxed hydrogel masks. They suit people whose skin you don't know, they pack small, and Olive Young or Daiso in Seoul sells all of them.

Hand creams are a visitor favorite at Olive Young. By the chain’s own count, visitors buy about 40% of its hand care.

That points to what makes a good beauty gift from Korea:

  • Works for any skin type. You don’t know your coworker’s skin.
  • Packs small. It has to survive your suitcase.
  • Feels like Seoul. It should be something they can’t grab at home.

Hand creams and masks check all three. Serums and full-size cleansers usually don’t.

Who gets what

  • Mom, aunt, host: W.DRESSROOM Perfume Hand Cream
  • Coworkers, a whole team: VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask, ₩1,000 each
  • The skincare friend: Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask
  • Someone who skips skincare: pumpkin tea or collagen (see the end)

Best for Almost Anyone: W.DRESSROOM Perfume Hand Cream

It smells like a perfume and works like a hand cream. Nobody needs to know their skin type to use it.

About 40% of Olive Young's hand care sales came from visitors, and the chain names perfume hand creams, W.DRESSROOM among them, as especially popular (Jan.–Aug. 2026).

Who it suits: Mom, an aunt, your host, a coworker you don't know well.

How to use: Rub a little into dry hands. Smell the tester first: the scent is the gift. Scents include No.49 Peach Blossom, No.30 White Musk and No.97 April Cotton.

Best for a Big Group: VT PDRN Glow Sheet Mask

₩1,000 a sheet at Daiso, so you can buy a stack. Each mask is sealed and flat.

Who it suits: Coworkers, classmates, a whole team.

How to use: After cleansing, leave it on for the time printed on the pouch. Peel it off and pat in the leftover essence. No rinsing.

Best for the Skincare Friend: Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask

Not a paper sheet: a two-piece hydrogel that stays on for hours and turns clear as it goes. A box holds four, so you can keep one and give three.

Who it suits: The friend with a ten-step routine.

How to use: Last step of the evening routine. Biodance suggests several hours or overnight, until the gel turns clear. Check the box for the exact time.

How to pack them

  • Carry-on (US flights): creams and gels must be 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less per container, all in one quart-size bag. A 100 ml hand cream fits.
  • Masks: they are soaked in essence. Put the stack in your checked bag, flat against the back panel.
  • Keep the seal: sealed boxes are easier at security and look ready to give.

Where to shop in Seoul

Olive Young for hand creams and boxed masks. Visitors now make up 33% of its in-store sales, and stores in busy tourist areas have staff who speak other languages.

Daiso for stacks of small gifts. Prices top out at ₩5,000.

Bring your passport. Tax-free shopping starts at ₩15,000 in one payment, and many tourist-area stores take the refund off at the register. (Amounts as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: Trip.com Korea Tax Refund Guide 2026. Rules can change, so check at the counter.)

Not into skincare? Try wellness gifts

Visitor spending on Olive Young's inner beauty shelf grew 64% in early 2026. Pumpkin tea and collagen are among the visitor favorites it names. Light to carry, no routine needed.

item.title: Olive Young Must-Buys: 4 K-Beauty Picks for First-Timers
item.description: New to Olive Young? Start with four Korean skin care picks that already sell well in the US, from pore pads to sunscreen, plus tips for shopping in Seoul.
item.content:encoded:
For a first Olive Young haul, start with four skin care picks that already sell well in the US: medicube Zero Pore Pad 2.0, Anua PDRN Hyaluronic Acid 100 Moisturizing Cream, Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask and Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen. Together they cover exfoliating, moisturizing, masking and sun care.

Olive Young is the first stop for most beauty shoppers in Seoul. Its big stores carry thousands of products, and the shelves change with the season.

So start with numbers. Three of the four picks below were on Amazon’s US Skin Care Best Sellers list on November 9, 2026. The fourth comes from Round Lab, one of the top three brands at Olive Young’s first US store in Pasadena.

That means you can try them at home before your trip, then restock in Seoul. Visitors now make up a third of Olive Young’s in-store sales, up from 2% in 2022.

What visitors buy

  • Over ₩1 trillion. That’s what visitors spent in Olive Young’s Korean stores from January to August 2026, according to the company.
  • Skin care first. It was the most popular category, ahead of makeup and hair care.
  • Derm-style skin care is growing. Visitor sales in that category rose about 78% from a year earlier.
  • Americans shop here too. The US was one of the top five countries by spending.

How to use this list

Treat it as a starter routine for your first visit, not a shopping spree. Each pick covers one step:

  • Exfoliate: medicube Zero Pore Pad 2.0
  • Moisturize: Anua PDRN Hyaluronic Acid 100 Moisturizing Cream
  • Mask: Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask, for a slow evening
  • Protect: Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen SPF 50, every morning

Already have a favorite for one of these steps? Skip it and use the suitcase space for something new.

In what order

  • Morning: pore pad, cream, sunscreen.
  • Evening: pore pad, cream. On a mask night, the mask goes on last.

Set a budget before you walk in

The average visitor buys 6 items, by Olive Young’s count. About 35% spend ₩100,000 or more in one payment.

Write your list first, one product per routine step. Buy what’s on it, then decide how much is left for extras.

Best Pore Pad: medicube Zero Pore Pad 2.0

Each pad has two sides: an embossed side to swipe first and a silky side to finish. The formula pairs lactic acid (AHA) with salicylic acid (BHA), so one pad gives you a quick exfoliating step and skin that looks smoother.

On Amazon US Skin Care Best Sellers, Nov 9, 2026 (#3 in the category that day).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants an easy exfoliating step. If your skin is very sensitive, medicube suggests starting a few times a week.

How to use: After cleansing, swipe the embossed side from the center of your face outward. Flip and swipe once more with the silky side, then pat in what's left. Keep it away from the eye area.

Best Moisturizer: Anua PDRN Hyaluronic Acid 100 Moisturizing Cream

A lightweight cream in a slim 60 ml tube that fits in a carry-on bag. Anua describes it as fast-absorbing and non-sticky, with a silky finish that doesn't pill under makeup. It pairs PDRN with hyaluronic acid for hydration and a natural-looking glow.

On Amazon US Skin Care Best Sellers, Nov 9, 2026 (#15 that day).

Who it suits: People who dislike heavy creams, or who want a moisturizer that sits well under makeup.

How to use: Use it morning and night as the last step of your skincare routine. In the morning, sunscreen goes on after it.

Best Sheet Mask: Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask

A hydrogel mask, not a paper sheet. It stays on for hours and turns clear as it goes, so it suits a slow evening more than a ten-minute break. Each box holds four masks, which makes it easy to share or pack.

On Amazon US Skin Care Best Sellers, Nov 9, 2026 (#9 that day).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants a quiet night in after a long day of walking around Seoul.

How to use: Make it the last step of your evening routine. Biodance suggests leaving it on for several hours or overnight, until the gel turns clear. Check the box for the exact time.

Best Sunscreen: Round Lab Birch Moisturizing Sunscreen SPF 50

A daily SPF 50 made with birch sap and hyaluronic acid. Round Lab describes it as lightweight and non-greasy with a dewy, moisturizer-like finish and no white cast.

Round Lab was one of the top three brands at Olive Young's first US store in Pasadena (Asia Economy, Aug 2026).

Who it suits: Anyone who skips sunscreen because it feels heavy or leaves a white cast.

How to use: Apply it liberally and evenly 15 minutes before you head out, as the last step of your morning routine.

How Olive Young works for visitors

  • Help in your language. Stores in busy tourist areas have staff who speak other languages and signs in several languages. Olive Young counts 151 of these stores nationwide.
  • Plan for more than one stop. In an Olive Young survey of visitors in May 2026, shoppers went to 2.8 stores on average. If one store is out of something, the next one may have it.

Tax-free shopping

  • Bring your passport. The physical one: photos and digital copies are often not accepted.
  • Spend ₩15,000 or more in one payment at a participating store to qualify.
  • Ask at the counter. Instant refunds cover up to ₩1,000,000 per receipt and ₩5,000,000 for your whole stay. You must be staying in Korea less than six months.
(Amounts as of Nov. 16, 2026. Source: Trip.com Korea Tax Refund Guide 2026. Rules can change, so check at the counter.)

If you only buy one thing

Make it the sunscreen. It's the one step you use every morning, at 50 ml it fits the US carry-on limit of 3.4 oz (100 ml), and Round Lab was one of the top three brands at Olive Young's US store.

If you already love your sunscreen, pick the pore pad instead. Seventy pads last a while.

item.title: Korean Pharmacy Skincare: Know What You're Buying
item.description: How to shop a Korean pharmacy as a visitor: cosmetics vs. functional cosmetics vs. medicines, what to ask the pharmacist, and one brightening pick.
item.content:encoded:
Most skincare in a Korean pharmacy is cosmetics, and some of it is functional cosmetics that Korea's drug regulator reviews for brightening, wrinkle or UV claims. Ointments and acne medications can be medicines, so ask the pharmacist before you buy them and check FDA rules before you bring any home.

Pharmacies in Myeongdong now sell almost as much skincare as medicine. In Seoul’s Jung District, home to Myeongdong, the number of pharmacies rose 20.9% in a year, to 214 in October 2026, Yonhap reported.

Visitors are the reason. Korea Tourism Data Lab estimates that foreign tourists’ spending at pharmacies jumped 196.1% in the first nine months of 2026. A pharmacist who opened a beauty-focused store in Myeongdong in February told Yonhap that nearly all customers were foreigners.

The catch: one shelf can hold a serum and a medicated ointment side by side. Here is how to tell them apart before you pay.

Three kinds of product on the shelf

  • Cosmetics: everyday skincare. Creams, cleansers, masks. No pharmacist needed.
  • Functional cosmetics (기능성화장품): still cosmetics, with a function defined by Korean law, such as helping brighten skin, improving wrinkles or protecting from UV rays. Each product must pass an evaluation by Korea’s Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) or be reported to it.
  • Medicines: acne medications, ointments and other drugs. They are medicine even when they sit next to the masks.

Why visitors shop here

  • Drug-company brands. Some Korean pharmaceutical companies run their own skincare lines. Dongkook Pharmaceutical, for one, launched Centellian24 in 2015.
  • Advice on the spot. Industry representatives say pharmacy beauty products appeal to shoppers who want specialized ingredients and professional advice.
  • Tax-free shopping. Many beauty pharmacies advertise it to international visitors. Bring your passport.

Where you’ll find beauty pharmacies

  • Myeongdong (Jung District): the biggest jump in Seoul, 20.9% more pharmacies in a year.
  • Hongdae (Mapo District): pharmacy numbers up 10.4%.
  • Seongsu (Seongdong District): up 9.4%.

Many of these stores look like cosmetics boutiques, with skincare up front and the counter at the back. Don’t let the layout decide for you. Check what kind of product you are holding.

Before you pay

  • Read the box, then ask. If you can’t tell whether something is a cosmetic or a medicine, ask. Simple Korean phrases are below.
  • Walk to a second shop. Pharmacies on the same street often carry the same lines, and some compete on price.
  • Mention what you already use. A pharmacist can only help with what they know about you.

What to buy, what to ask about

  • Buy freely: cosmetics and functional cosmetics, like the brightening ampoule below.
  • Ask first: anything labeled as medicine, and any ointment or acne product. The pharmacist decides whether it suits you, not a shopping list.

Best for a Brightening Step: Easydew DW-EGF Melatoning Oneday Ampoule

A brightening-focused ampoule from Easydew, a line its Korean store sells as Daewoong Pharmaceutical's Easydew. It is a cosmetic, so you can take it off the shelf without a pharmacist. Olive Young carries it too, which makes it easy to compare prices. The formula pairs niacinamide, a familiar brightening ingredient, with the brand's own EGF.

Easydew said the ampoule sold 800,000 bottles in the nine months after launch (brand figures reported by Pharmnews, April 2023).

Who it suits: Anyone who wants a brightening step for a more even-looking tone. If your skin is sensitive, try it on a small area first.

How to use: Apply a small amount to the areas you want to look more even and massage until absorbed. Easydew suggests using it morning and night.

Pharmacy or Olive Young?

Same product, two kinds of store. This ampoule is sold in pharmacies and on Olive Young's Korean site. Check both before you pay.

Prices move. Myeongdong pharmacies compete hard on price, Korea Bizwire reports, so the first shop on the street is not always the cheapest.

Staff may not be pharmacists. Many beauty pharmacies employ more sales assistants than pharmacists. For anything that could be medicine, ask for the pharmacist.

Back home: Easydew runs a US online store, so you can reorder later.

How to ask a Korean pharmacist

  • "약사님 계세요?" (yak-sa-nim gye-se-yo?) Is the pharmacist here?
  • "이거 화장품이에요, 약이에요?" (i-geo hwa-jang-pum-i-e-yo, yak-i-e-yo?) Is this a cosmetic or a medicine?
  • "기능성화장품이에요?" (gi-neung-seong hwa-jang-pum-i-e-yo?) Is this a functional cosmetic?
  • "택스 리펀 돼요?" (taek-seu ri-peon dwae-yo?) Can I get a tax refund?

If words fail, show a photo of the product on your phone. Tell the pharmacist about allergies and any medicine you already take.

Medicines: what not to do

  • Don't buy medicine from a shopping list. Ointments and acne medications can be drugs. Ask the pharmacist whether one suits you, rather than buying because a video said so.
  • Don't assume the rules match. A Korean Pharmaceutical Association representative noted that some medicines sold without a prescription in Korea may face different rules overseas.
  • Know the US rule. The FDA says that in most circumstances it is illegal for individuals to bring drugs into the US for personal use, because many have not been approved there. Read its personal importation page before you pack any medicine.
